title: Exponent transport of normalized integration and bounded tensor adjoints
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions], put $A=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$, and let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without assuming $S$ separated over $k$. For every scheme $T$ used below, work in the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on its small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] and derived tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, write $L_{T,r}=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$, and use the root-projection comparison $C_TL_{T,r}\cong A_T(1)$ and its tensor powers [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For a separated finite-type map $f:X\to Y$ with compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$, let $F_f^e=Rp_{e,*}j_!^e$ and $F_f^p=Rp_{p,*}j_!^p$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Use precisely $B_f=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j_!}:C_YF_f^e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_f^pC_X$, where $\beta$ is the counit-mate comparison and $e_j$ the adjoint extension comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison].
Let $\pi:V\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. For each annihilating exponent $r$, suppose $t_{\pi,r}^e:F_\pi^eL_{V,r}^{\otimes d}[2d]\to A_S$ is the ordinary integration [def-amb-vector-integration], and $t_{\pi,r}^p:F_\pi^pA_V(d)[2d]\to A_S$ is obtained by degree-zero gluing of the ordered affine-line integrations constructed from the supported Kummer projective trace, i.e. the map of [def-pur-proetale-vector-integration] built from [def-pur-supported-projective-site-arrows, def-pur-proetale-ordered-integration, def-pur-proetale-frame-integration] (these definition nodes index the coefficient ring as $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n'+1}$ and the exponent by $\ell^{r'+1}A=0$; take $n'=n-1$, $r'=r-1$). Suppose their actual maps compare by $t_{\pi,r}^p B_\pi=C_S(t_{\pi,r}^e)$ for every $r$, using the same chosen projective completion and root comparisons. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], set $J_r=\pi_e^*K\otimes_A^LL_{V,r}^{\otimes d}[2d]$ and let $a_{K,r}^e:F_\pi^eJ_r\to K$ and $a_{C_SK,r}^p:F_\pi^pC_VJ_r\to C_SK$ be the canonical inverse compact-support projection followed by $1\otimes t_{\pi,r}$ [def-exchange-projection, def-kun-projection-formula-map], in the coordinates of [def-pur-vector-integration-adjunction-arrows, def-pur-proetale-vector-integration-arrows, def-pur-finite-site-tensor-projection]. Write $\eta_{K,r}^e$ and $\eta_{C_SK,r}^p$ for their transposes under the ordinary compact-support adjunction and the bounded etale-origin adjunction [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $\rho_K:C_V\pi^{\times,e}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi^!C_SK$ be induced by the comparison unit $K\cong R\nu_{S,*}C_SK$, and form the bounded site transpose, as in [def-pur-bounded-site-transpose-arrows]; the equations below are the predicate of [def-pur-vector-tensor-site-equations].
The specified comparisons identify the actual compact-support projection maps, and
$$a_{C_SK,r}^p B_{\pi,J_r}=C_S(a_{K,r}^e),\qquad \eta_{C_SK,r}^p=\rho_K C_V(\eta_{K,r}^e).$$
The transpose is invertible and its inverse is the transported inverse of the ordinary integration adjoint, hence the integration-normalized vector-bundle purity identification [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity, cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity, def-pur-vector-purity-normalization]. All transposes here have bounded-below etale witnesses, including $\pi^{\times,e}K$; no unbounded ambient pro-etale exceptional adjunction is asserted.
For $s\geq r$ killing $A$, use the canonical transition $L_{T,s}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{T,r}$ induced by $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{s-r}}$, the exponent transition of [def-pur-finite-site-coordinates]. Under this transition the actual projective unit-Chern decompositions, their inverse traces and open restrictions, all ordered affine traces, the glued vector traces, the coefficient integration maps, their adjunction transposes and inverse purity maps at $s$ and $r$ agree. Thus every displayed comparison is independent of the annihilating exponent. These conclusions hold for $d=0$ and empty $S$ and impose no condition $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ or flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$.

proof.text: Finite type over the field gives Noetherianity. The coefficient prime is a unit in every stalk by the coefficient-setting theorem, hence in global sections by the local unit criterion.

Apply the forward projective exponent squares. Insert the two decomposition inverses to obtain q followed by b_r inverse = b_s inverse followed by biprod.map(e,identity). Compose with the second projection to obtain the actual trace equality. This is decomposition_of_square in the Lean.

Step 2 works for every Noetherian base with the prime invertible. Supply that entire family to affine exponent transport, so that it also applies at the recursive affine prefixes. For the vector equation, use the existing pro-etale exponent-independence declaration. Naturality of compactSupportSiteComparison inverse carries this equality into comparison of the ordinary equation, by the assumed trace comparison at r and s. Full faithfulness with bounded constant target (the Hom bijection of comparison on a bounded-below target) reflects that ordinary equation.

At each exponent use the existing single-exponent tensor data. Ordinary adjunct invertibility defines etaE, and transfers the lower bound of J to its target. The comparison unit on bounded K is invertible; apply the exceptional functor and comparison to obtain exactly rho. Define etaP as comparison of etaE followed by rho. The tensor data transpose square gives its prescribed bounded transpose formula; its inverse is the reversed composite.

Apply inverse-projection naturality to the two transpose data. Postcompose with the tensor of each global vector trace and the right unitor. Functor.map_comp and the vector trace equations give both coefficient integration transitions. Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left gives i.hom followed by etaE_r.hom = etaE_s.hom. The transpose equations and the common prescribed rho formula give the identical pro-etale equation. Cancel the isomorphisms to get etaE_r.inv followed by i.inv = etaE_s.inv and its pro-etale version. Assemble the projective, affine, vector and tensor predicates without modifying any conclusion.
